cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: A food allergy is an immune system reaction to a specific food protein; symptoms can be severe and include anaphylaxis (a life-threatening reaction).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: A food intolerance is a non-immune adverse reaction to food; symptoms are usually less severe and include bloating, diarrhoea, and stomach cramps.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition where gluten damages the small intestine lining, preventing nutrient absorption. Sufferers must follow a strict gluten-free diet.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose (milk sugar) due to a lack of the enzyme lactase; symptoms include bloating and diarrhoea after consuming dairy.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Common food allergies include: peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, soy, wheat, celery, and sesame.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Vegetarians do not eat meat, poultry, or fish; types include lacto-ovo (eat dairy and eggs), lacto (eat dairy), and ovo (eat eggs).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Vegans exclude all animal products including meat, dairy, eggs, honey, and often avoid animal-derived additives like gelatine and rennet.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Religious diets: Muslims follow Halal, Jews follow Kosher, Hindus often avoid beef and many are vegetarian, Sikhs may avoid Halal meat.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: Medical diets include: diabetic (controlled sugar and carbohydrate intake), low-sodium (for high blood pressure), low-fat (for heart disease), and high-fibre (for bowel health).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Special Diets & Food Intolerance
cards.back: When adapting recipes for special diets, substitutions must maintain nutritional balance: e.g. replacing wheat flour with gluten-free blends, using plant milk instead of dairy, or using eggs alternatives like aquafaba or flaxseed.

cards.front: What should you know about food preparation & nutrition exam tips — special diets & food intolerance?
cards.back: 1. For Special Diets & Food Intolerance questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Special Diets & Food Intolerance question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method
